sourcedFrom: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: The Cx4 is a blowback carbine that splits into upper and stock on one cross-pin, and the cocking handle is the part that holds the bolt in. ⛔ Once the handle is out the bolt is loose and can simply fall — Beretta warns about it in as many words, and it is a heavy part landing on a hard floor.

steps.title: Unloaded, and memorise how it sits before it moves
steps.action: Certain the carbine is unloaded, per the load-check instructions. Then look at how the parts sit before you take any of them out — Beretta asks for that explicitly on this gun, and the bolt/cocking-handle relationship is not obvious once it is in pieces.
steps.aside: Before disas- sembling the parts, carefully observe and memorize the position of the components to facilitate their correct reassembly.
steps.quote: Always be cer- tain that the carbine is unloaded. Please refer to the instructions given in the ”load check” paragraph.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Magazine out, then COCK the hammer
steps.action: Push the magazine release and take the magazine out. Then cock the hammer — retract the bolt by the cocking handle and ease the bolt back to the closed position. Beretta advises it because the strip is easier with the hammer out of the way.
steps.aside: Remove the magazine by pushing the magazine release button.
steps.quote: To facilitate disassembly, it is advisable to cock the hammer. Retract the bolt by means of the cocking handle and gently take the bolt to the closed position.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Disassembly latch out — either side will do
steps.action: Push the disassembly latch out of the carbine's frame. It can be driven out from either side, which is the one genuinely ambidextrous thing about the strip.
steps.aside: The disassembly latch can be removed from either side.
steps.quote: Push the disassembly latch out the frame of the carbine.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Receiver/barrel assembly off the stock
steps.action: Slide the front part of the carbine — the receiver/barrel assembly — forward off the stock. The stock is the lower receiver on this gun and it stays behind with the trigger group in it.
steps.quote: Slide the front part of the carbine (receiver/barrel assembly) from the stock.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20-21

steps.title: ⛔ Cocking handle out — and now the bolt is loose
steps.action: Retract the cocking handle fully until it lines up with the circular part of its port, then pull it out FORCEFULLY. ⛔ At that moment nothing is holding the bolt: it is no longer blocked in position and can fall out of the receiver. Have a hand under it before you pull the handle, then take the bolt out of the barrel. Strip complete.
steps.aside: Fully retract the cocking handle until it corresponds with the opening (circular part) of the port.
steps.quote: At this stage, the bolt is not blocked into position by the cocking handle and could therefore fall out. Handle with care all disassembled parts.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, on a rod
steps.action: Oil on a brush, in from the CHAMBER side on a rod long enough to go through, and scrub chamber and bore. Solvent first if it needs it, then patches on the rod until one emerges clean, then a light oil inside and outside. ⛔ Check the bore is clear of obstructions before it goes back.
steps.aside: Check the bar- rel to be sure there are no obstructions in the chamber and bore.
steps.quote: Insert he brush into the barrel by means of a rod from the chamber and scrub the chamber and bore thoroughly.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — CLEANING, printed p.40-41

steps.title: Bolt: breech face, extractor, EJECTOR and the guides
steps.action: Patch with gun oil over the bolt, with attention to the breech face, the extractor, the EJECTOR and the bolt guides. The ejector is on the bolt on this carbine and it is reversible, which means it is also the part that collects fouling in a corner nobody looks at.
steps.quote: Clean the bolt with a patch and Beretta oil or a good grade gun oil, paying special attention to the breech face, extractor, ejector and to the bolt guides.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — CLEANING, printed p.40-41

steps.title: Receiver, stock, and a magazine that goes back DRY
steps.action: Synthetic wire brush over every area with powder residue, then wipe the outer receiver and stock surfaces clean. The magazine must be thoroughly clean with a follower that slides freely; oil the internal walls only if it needs it and then ⛔ run a DRY patch through — no lubricant is left inside the magazine box.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the box. Do not leave lubricant inside the magazine box.
steps.quote: Using a synthetic wire brush clean all areas covered by gunpowder residue and dirt.
steps.cite: Beretta Cx4 Storm Carbine User Manual — UT007448/00 (form code printed in the running header) — CLEANING, printed p.40-41

deepAbsentReason: Beretta publishes nothing past this strip for a Cx4 owner. The one deeper operation the book describes — reversing the safety and magazine release buttons — it assigns away in a footnote: "This operation should be carried out by a gunsmith." A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so it is carried as a prohibition rather than a deep-clean branch and nothing is borrowed from elsewhere to fill the gap.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush on a rod, in from the CHAMBER end
Solvent first if needed, then patches until one emerges clean
Light oil inside and outside; ⛔ bore checked clear before reassembly

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Breech face, extractor, ejector and bolt guides
Brush if it needs it, then wiped with a clean patch and lightly oiled

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING & GUIDE
tasks: Lightly oiled; scoured with a brush first after long use

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, STOCK & MAGAZINE
tasks: Synthetic wire brush over powder residue, outer surfaces wiped clean
Magazine follower must slide freely under thumb pressure
⛔ Dry patch through the magazine box — no lubricant left inside

reassembly: Check the hammer is cocked; if not, pull the trigger fully and hold it, draw the hammer back and release the trigger.
Bolt onto the barrel with the bolt's lower guides matched to the receiver's lower guides.
Line the hole in the bolt body up with the rear (circular) part of the cocking port.
Cocking handle in with the CONCAVE part facing the barrel, pushed into the hole of the bolt and then fully forward until it stops.
Stock's side rails engaged with the receiver/barrel/bolt assembly's side rails, then slid on until it stops.
Disassembly latch pushed into its seat while holding stock and receiver together.
Pull the trigger to decock the hammer.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: retract the bolt to confirm it moves freely, check the cocking handle is pushed fully forward until it stops, and confirm the disassembly latch is seated. Then pull the trigger to decock the hammer, as the book's own reassembly ends. ⛔ Note that with an EMPTY magazine inserted the bolt stays open on retraction — press the bolt release lever downward to close it, fingers clear of the ejection port.
